original_question: For a finite group G let Cod(G) denote the set of irreducible character codegrees of G(see 20.78). Define σ(G) = max{|π(m)|: m ∈ Cod(G)}, where π(m) denotes the set of prime divisors of an integer m. It is proved that there exists a constant k such that |π(G)| ⩽ k · σ(G) for every finite group G(Y. Yang, G. Qian, J. Algebra, 478(2017), 215–219), but the estimate provided for k is very crude. Can the constant k be taken as 4?
target_in_paper: Open Problem 21.108 in Section 21 of The Kourovka Notebook (21st issue, 2026), with notation imported from Open Problem 20.78, is the exact target of your draft. Your wording is essentially the same question as the official problem. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the official problem almost verbatim: it is about finite groups, uses Cod(G), defines the quantity σ(G) from prime divisors of codegrees, recalls the Yang–Qian 2017 existence of a universal linear bound, and asks exactly whether the constant can be chosen to be 4. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))

You should specify that the characters involved are irreducible complex characters; that is part of the definition in 20.78 and is only implicit in your draft. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/20tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))

You should define π(G) explicitly as π(|G|), the set of prime divisors of |G|. Problem 21.108 uses π(G) without reintroducing it, so this is needed for a self-contained formulation. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))

It should be stated explicitly that the proposed inequality with constant 4 is meant to hold for every finite group G, with no extra hypotheses such as solvability, simplicity, or nilpotency. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))

The cross-reference “see 20.78” should be removed in a stand-alone version and replaced by the actual notation and definitions from 20.78. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/20tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))
refined_question: Let G be a finite group, let Irr(G) be the set of irreducible complex characters of G, and for χ∈Irr(G) define the codegree cod(χ)=|G:ker χ|/χ(1). Set Cod(G)={cod(χ):χ∈Irr(G)}. If π(n) denotes the set of prime divisors of a positive integer n and π(G)=π(|G|), define σ(G)=max{|π(m)|:m∈Cod(G)}. Is it true that |π(G)|≤4σ(G) for every finite group G? ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))
justification: This draft is not trying to restate Problem 20.78 itself (which is the element-order divisibility conjecture for codegrees) or Problem 20.79 (the codegree-set recognition conjecture for simple groups). Rather, it matches the later Open Problem 21.108, which explicitly asks whether the universal constant k from the Yang–Qian bound can be taken to be 4, while pointing back to 20.78 only for the definition of codegrees. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))
